parameters.name: thread
parameters.label: Threads (--thread)
parameters.help_text: Number of CPU cores. Set to -1 to use all available cores.

parameters.name: auto
parameters.label: Auto strategy (--auto)
parameters.help_text: Pick an appropriate algorithm strategy based on dataset size. Overrides the strategy choice below.

parameters.name: strategy
parameters.label: Pairwise alignment strategy
parameters.help_text: Mutually exclusive accuracy strategies. Ignored if Auto is on.

parameters.name: maxiterate
parameters.label: Iterative refinement (--maxiterate)
parameters.help_text: Number of refinement iterations (0 = none). Recommended 1000 with --localpair/--globalpair for small inputs.

parameters.name: adjustdirection
parameters.label: Adjust strand direction (--adjustdirection)
parameters.help_text: Automatically detect and reverse-complement nucleotide sequences that are in the wrong direction. Fast heuristic check.

parameters.name: retree
parameters.label: Guide tree rebuilds (--retree)
parameters.help_text: How many times to rebuild the guide tree. 1 = fastest.

parameters.name: seqtype
parameters.label: Sequence type
parameters.help_text: Force input alphabet when auto-detection fails.

parameters.name: bl
parameters.label: BLOSUM matrix (--bl)
parameters.help_text: Substitution matrix for protein alignment. BLOSUM62 is the MAFFT default; use 30/45 for divergent sequences, 80 for closely related. Overridden by JTT or TM if set.

parameters.name: jtt
parameters.label: JTT PAM matrix (--jtt)
parameters.help_text: Use JTT PAM matrix instead of BLOSUM. Enter the PAM number (e.g. 200). Leave empty to use BLOSUM.

parameters.name: tm
parameters.label: Transmembrane PAM matrix (--tm)
parameters.help_text: Use transmembrane PAM matrix instead of BLOSUM. Enter the PAM number (e.g. 200). Leave empty to use BLOSUM. Designed for transmembrane proteins.

parameters.name: op
parameters.label: Gap opening penalty (--op)
parameters.help_text: Penalty for opening a gap. Default 1.53.

parameters.name: ep
parameters.label: Gap offset (--ep)
parameters.help_text: Offset that behaves like a gap extension penalty. Default 0.0.

parameters.name: adjustdirectionaccurately
parameters.label: Adjust strand direction accurately (--adjustdirectionaccurately)
parameters.help_text: Like --adjustdirection but uses a more accurate (and slower) algorithm. Recommended when direction detection matters.

parameters.name: fmodel
parameters.label: Use scoring model (--fmodel)
parameters.help_text: Incorporate the AA/nuc composition of each sequence into the scoring model.

parameters.name: lop
parameters.label: Local gap open penalty (--lop)
parameters.help_text: Gap open penalty for the local pairwise alignment stage.

parameters.name: lep
parameters.label: Local gap extension penalty (--lep)
parameters.help_text: Gap extension penalty for the local pairwise alignment stage.

parameters.name: lexp
parameters.label: Local gap offset (--lexp)
parameters.help_text: Offset for the local pairwise alignment stage.

parameters.name: weighti
parameters.label: Consistency weight (--weighti)
parameters.help_text: Weighting factor for the consistency term calculated from pairwise alignments. Default 2.7.

parameters.name: LOP
parameters.label: Skip-alignment gap open (--LOP)
parameters.help_text: Gap opening penalty to skip the alignment in L-INS-i / E-INS-i. Default -6.00.

parameters.name: LEXP
parameters.label: Skip-alignment gap extension (--LEXP)
parameters.help_text: Gap extension penalty to skip the alignment in L-INS-i / E-INS-i. Default 0.00.

parameters.name: nofft
parameters.label: Disable FFT (--nofft)
parameters.help_text: Turn off the FFT-based homology search. Slower but sometimes more stable on short sequences.

parameters.name: parttree
parameters.label: PartTree guide tree (--parttree)
parameters.help_text: Use the PartTree algorithm for the guide tree with 6mer distance. Suitable for very large datasets (>50 000 sequences). Mutually exclusive with --dpparttree.

parameters.name: dpparttree
parameters.label: DP PartTree guide tree (--dpparttree)
parameters.help_text: Use PartTree algorithm with distance-programming-based distances. More accurate than --parttree but slower. Mutually exclusive with --parttree.

parameters.name: partsize
parameters.label: PartTree partition size (--partsize)
parameters.help_text: Number of partitions in the PartTree algorithm. Only used when --parttree or --dpparttree is enabled. Default 50.

parameters.name: groupsize
parameters.label: Max group size (--groupsize)
parameters.help_text: Do not make alignment larger than this number of sequences. Useful with --parttree for extremely large inputs. Leave empty for no limit.

parameters.name: noscore
parameters.label: Skip alignment score (--noscore)
parameters.help_text: Skip the alignment score check. Can speed up the run on large inputs.

parameters.name: memsave
parameters.label: Memory-saving mode (--memsave)
parameters.help_text: Use less memory at the expense of speed. Useful for very large datasets.

parameters.name: pileup
parameters.label: Pileup alignment (--pileup)
parameters.help_text: Align sequences sequentially in input order instead of using a guide tree. Simple and fast but less accurate.

parameters.name: large
parameters.label: Large dataset mode (--large)
parameters.help_text: Use files instead of RAM for temporary data. Slower but avoids memory exhaustion on very large datasets.

parameters.name: memsavetree
parameters.label: Memory-saving guide tree (--memsavetree)
parameters.help_text: Use less memory to build the guide tree. Useful for datasets with many sequences.

parameters.name: anysymbol
parameters.label: Accept non-standard symbols (--anysymbol)
parameters.help_text: Allow non-standard characters in input sequences (e.g. U in protein). Without this flag, MAFFT may reject unusual symbols.

parameters.name: reorder
parameters.label: Reorder output (--reorder)
parameters.help_text: Reorder output by alignment order rather than input order.

parameters.name: treeout
parameters.label: Save guide tree (--treeout)
parameters.help_text: Write the guide tree alongside the alignment. The tree file is not displayed in the UI but is produced on disk.
